title.narrative: Integrated Cholera Response through Case Management and Community-Led Action with provison of lifesaving health and nutrition services among conflict affected people in Tawila, North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project was originally designed in response to the cholera outbreak triggered by the April 2025 attacks on Zamzam IDP camp, which displaced nearly 500,000 people, with over 327,000 arriving in Tawila locality. The sudden population influx overwhelmed public services and widened critical WASH gaps, causing a rapidly escalating outbreak. ALIMA responded by scaling up Cholera Treatment Units and Centres, establishing Oral Rehydration Points, and implementing Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities targeting 24,000 conflict-affected people.ltbrgtAs cholera cases declined significantly, ALIMA reprogrammed the project in a first amendment toward integrated health and nutrition services, while maintaining cholera surveillance and preparedness. The reprogrammed intervention expanded equitable access to outpatient curative care, basic sexual and reproductive health services, and community-based nutrition services targeting severe acute malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women across six sites in Tawila locality: Umda, Daba Nyara, Rwanda B, Tabramarara, Al Jami East, and Shockshoko. The project continues to contribute directly to Health and Nutrition Cluster strategic objectives by strengthening life-saving service delivery, reinforcing local capacity through training and mentorship of MoH staff and community health workers, and improving emergency preparedness and resilience among conflict-affected populations.ltbrgtThis second amendment maintains all current health and nutrition activities and expands the project to two additional operational locations: Garni PHC in El Fasher Locality and Katur PHCC in Tawila Locality. The expansion follows the unexpected withdrawal of MSF Franceltbrgtfrom Garni PHC and MSF Spain from Katur PHCC, creating an immediate critical gap in primary healthcare services for displaced and conflict-affected populations. Both facilities retain MSF-trained staff whom ALIMA will engage and retain, ensuring continuity and quality of care from day one. As part of the handover, MSF agencies will provide a portion of medical supplies to support the transition. No additional funding is requested project savings will be reallocated to cover expansion costs including medicines replenishment and minor facility repairs.ltbrgtA no-cost extension (NCE) is also requested to allow ALIMA adequate time to mobilise follow-on funding from multiple sources and ensure uninterrupted service continuity beyond the current project end date of 13 September 2026. ALIMA is actively pursuing funding for continuation, including through the SHF SA1 2026 cycle under which both Garni and Katur are included as target sites. ltbrgtlt/pgt
